R2-01.why: It has all three things that make clips: fear (Mom hunting), betrayal (snitching) and chaos (smashing the house). The thumbnail of a trashed house, a furious parent and a kid stuffing a cake into the piano matches the gameplay exactly, and the FREEZE! catch makes sense in 15 seconds with no context.
R2-01.fix: Make the Report Card a one-tap vertical clip export with the gasp freeze-frame. Make sure PARTY-phase destruction is visually huge (client debris plus a server-visible mess state) so the before/after contrast reads in a thumbnail.

R2-02.why: Six people fighting over one raft and spinning into a waterfall is instantly readable chaos, and the WHO SANK US? blame card invites friends to argue and share. But it has no fear or betrayal, and the clips are mostly the same wipeout repeated, so it is funny without much surprise.
R2-02.fix: Add a griefing/betrayal lever (e.g., a secret 'saboteur seat' mutator, or letting a player bail water INTO the raft) and a dramatic slow-mo waterfall freeze-frame with the blamed player highlighted.

R2-03.why: The guard's flashlight sweeping over a statue frozen in an absurd pose off its plinth is tense and funny at the same time, and Red Light Green Light reads with no context. The pranks (helmet on the T-rex, a moustache on the portrait) make great screenshots, and hide-in-plain-sight games already have a proven creator audience.
R2-03.fix: Make freeze poses comedic and player-chosen from an emote wheel so a frozen statue mid-dab next to the T-rex becomes the signature image. Add a slow-mo 'almost caught' replay in the Caught on Camera reel.

R2-04.why: Fusion banners and the rubber-chicken misfire are fun moments, but the players are fixed turrets on a balcony, so there is no human slapstick or betrayal. A tower-defence screen full of VFX looks generic as a thumbnail and to someone watching a stream.
R2-04.fix: Allow friendly-fire fusions (firenado launches a teammate off the balcony) and give the misfire table player-facing consequences. Show the drawn runes big on screen so viewers see the 'bad drawing -> chicken' joke.

R2-05.why: Social deduction has proven creator appeal, and the reveals (the fossil is chicken bones, the MADE IN 2026 sticker) are good punchlines. But inspecting items with tools is slow, the payoff needs a whole round of context, and with pings/emotes only the accusation drama loses its voice.
R2-05.fix: Make the forger reveal an animated 'unmasking' moment where the forger's avatar gets dramatically exposed at the meeting, and add a physical caught-in-the-act state (forger seen in the back room) that makes a 15-second clip.

R2-06.why: Jump-scare chases and 'the Watcher saw it, you didn't' moments create real fear reactions, and the anomaly genre has a big audience on YouTube. But the clips are hard to tell apart from dozens of motel/anomaly games, and a CCTV thumbnail grid is not a distinctive visual identity.
R2-06.fix: Give the motel a signature monster/mascot for thumbnails and let the Watcher lie with pings in an optional 'Liar Shift' mode, which adds betrayal on top of fear.

R2-07.why: The game's whole purpose is making clips: a built-in replay of the crew being dragged off, with fake comments, is shareable by design and fits creators. But Content Warning's virality depended on proximity voice, which most Roblox under-16 players will not have, and the ghost-hunt visuals are crowded.
R2-07.fix: Record and replay emote/ragdoll and exaggerated scream-face animations, plus auto-captions from pings, so replays stay funny without voice. Add a one-tap export of the 30 s replay in vertical format with the fake-comments outro.

R2-08.why: A wedding cake splatting on the doorstep or a baby dragon waking up mid-hallway is readable physical comedy, and the value meter dropping gives a clear stakes visual. Scripted, server-tagged physics risks feeling less emergent than TRDS-style ragdoll chaos, which caps how surprising the outcomes can be.
R2-08.fix: Guarantee a spectacular failure state for every parcel (aquarium bursts and fish flop everywhere, the dragon torches the porch) and add a slow-mo 'tip lost' instant replay. Lean on Versus banana-peel sabotage for betrayal clips.

R2-09.why: Weird three-headed mutant critters are screenshot-worthy show-offs, but auto-battle fights on a 3x3 board have little spectator appeal and need explanation. The chaos and funny human moments that drive short-form clips are mostly absent.
R2-09.fix: Make mutations absurd and visible in combat (a three-headed critter argues with itself, a fish-tailed critter flops) and add a 'gremlin revenge' highlight when knocked-out players wreck a leader's board.

R2-10.why: Keep Talking clips are funny because of the panicked yelling, but a pictographic stamp relay removes exactly that. Watching someone tap matching symbols is not clip material, though the confetti-blast fail launching both players out the window is a nice closer.
R2-10.fix: Make the failure blast huge and ragdoll both players through the town. Add a 'wrong stamp' reaction emote and a 10-second countdown panic visual so the tension reads without voice.

R2-11.why: A burning airship with crew running between fires and then crashing spectacularly makes an obvious, readable thumbnail and a chaotic clip. But Overcooked-style crisis is better to play than to watch, and Land or Die / Survive the Plane Crash already own similar imagery.
R2-11.fix: Make crashes the star: varied, absurd crash landings (into a cow farm, a stadium), a crash-cam replay, and a 'who let the fire spread' blame card to add friend-group blame.

R2-12.why: Collapsing floors and last-second rescues of a panicked elephant calf are good wholesome-chaos moments, and the thumbnail (firefighter carrying a puppy out of flames) is clear. But there is no betrayal or player-vs-player hook, and firefighting PvE clips tend to look like ordinary sim gameplay.
R2-12.fix: Add an opt-in comedic failure (a critter escapes and causes mayhem, an elephant sprays the team) and a rescue-cam slow-mo for floor-collapse saves. Make the sanctuary hose fight a headline social activity.

overall_notes: The concepts with human-vs-human tension and readable physical comedy (R2-01 GROUNDED!, R2-03 STATUE SHUFFLE) clearly lead on virality. Co-op chaos concepts (R2-02, R2-07, R2-08, R2-11) sit in the solid 7 band: funny but with little betrayal or fear. Concepts whose fun relies on voice (R2-05, R2-07, R2-10) lose a lot under Roblox's age-gated chat and need emote/visual substitutes. Auto-battler and turret-style input (R2-09, R2-04) have weak spectator appeal. Several concepts already include replay/report features. The biggest cross-cutting improvement would be one-tap vertical clip export of those built-in highlight reels.
